title: Lester's army trouble and his white wife Mary
summary: Lee says Lester's commanding officer was right that the wife in the locker photo was white, and that Lester could not adjust to orders.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: There is a discrepancy which is not of great importance, but I found it in several books -- references to the unhappy experience that Lester had in the army. And there are several versions -- but one of the things that they say infuriated his commanding officer was supposedly finding a picture of his wife in his locker, and Leonard Feather says he was married to a white woman, Dan Morganstern says he was married to a black woman who was very light skinned, but that the commanding officer thought he was married to a white woman, and therefore, punished Lester. Is this all true?

Well, the commanding officer was right. She was a white woman. You know, she was not a light skinned black woman; she was a white woman. Her name was Mary, and they'd been married for several years ... several years, and I heard the story, but you also have to remember about Lester, as I told you, about his childhood.
